assertions.name: correction_tower_convergent_term_ratios
assertions.source: MEASURED convergence of the ℏ_q tower at q₀, replacing `correction_tower_converges` (computed=1/expected=1, green regardless of the numbers — bean qou-26f2). A convergent series evaluated at a point needs its successive TERM magnitudes to decrease; here 0 of the 2 successive ratios are < 1. Terms: |ℏ³| = 0.000972704, then |c₄ℏ⁴| = 115.335 (×118571.0) and |c₅ℏ⁵| = 115.335 (×1.0). So the tower DIVERGES at q₀ beyond the ℏ³ term and expected=0 records that honest negative — it goes red the moment a reconstruction actually produces decreasing terms, which is the alarm worth having. The ℏ³ term itself is genuine and is the module's one real result: it improves the residual from -1431.2717 ppm to -459.96026 ppm. The 2×2 ℏ⁴/ℏ⁵ solve is well conditioned (cond ≈ 300), so the ~1e6 coefficients are real, not numerical noise; see `two_term_fit.caveat`. computed = -1 means the 2×2 solve raised and the tower could not be measured at all — red, not a vacuous 0-of-0 pass; `two_term_fit.solve_error` then carries the reason.

description: Reconstructs the exact flavor-split correction tower: X = X_leading · (1 + ℏ_q³ + c₄ℏ⁴ + c₅ℏ⁵ + ...) where ℏ_q = (q-1)/q is the substrate Planck constant. Identifies the coefficient c₄ and checks for rational structure.

two_term_fit.caveat: 2 equations, 2 unknowns — the fit INTERPOLATES the two sample points exactly, so its residual at q₀ is ~0 by construction and is not evidence of convergence. The rhs moves from 4.6e-4 to 14.66 across a 9% change in ℏ_q, so the residual being fitted is not a smooth low-order polynomial in ℏ_q over that span.
